description:
Concurrent jit operations fail on lock contention instead of queueing, and a gate checker's finished verdict can be discarded. Every lock acquisition gives up after 5 s. An adopter repository whose mutations hold the lock for several seconds therefore has to serialize, stagger, and retry every tracker call.

## Background

A mutation holds the repository lock chain (worktree bootstrap, bootstrap, repository write, events) while it captures and publishes. Every acquisition in that chain waits for `LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECS` (5 s), or for `JIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` when set, and then fails. The claims-coordination lock and the claim commands use the 5 s constant and ignore `JIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT`. In an adopter repository where one mutation held the lock for 6 to 18 s, a concurrent `doc add`, `issue update`, or `gate evaluate` reliably failed with `Lock timeout`.

`gate evaluate` releases the lock chain while an external checker runs and re-acquires it to record the verdict. If that re-acquisition times out, the command returns an error, and the checker's completed result is dropped without a gate run, status update, or event. A 30-minute review that happens to finish during another mutation is lost.

A lock timeout is not classified. It exits `1` (generic error) on most commands and `6` (`GATE_ERROR`, already exists) from `gate evaluate --json`, so automation cannot tell contention apart from a real failure.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: With no configuration, a lock acquisition waits at least 60 s before failing.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every file lock jit acquires, including claims coordination and the claim commands, resolves its wait from `JIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` through one shared resolver.
- [hard] REQ-03: When an external checker has finished, a lock timeout while re-acquiring the repository locks is retried until the locks are acquired. The completed verdict is then recorded.
- [hard] REQ-04: A lock-acquisition timeout exits with a dedicated exit code, and in `--json` mode reports a dedicated error code, on every command including `gate evaluate`.
- [hard] REQ-05: Two mutations started concurrently both succeed when each holds the lock for less than the configured wait.

## Notes

A gate evaluation that times out before its checker starts has no lock under which to record a "not started" run. The dedicated exit code is the signal that the gate was not evaluated.

Reducing how long a mutation holds the lock is tracked separately.
title: Concurrent jit operations fail on lock contention instead of waiting
